related.name: Audio Dynamic Range & Data Rate Calculator

method: Microphone sensitivity is quoted at 1 kHz with 1 pascal of sound pressure, and 1 Pa is 94 dB SPL. A figure in mV/Pa is the open-circuit output voltage at that reference; dBV/Pa is the same ratio as 20 log10 of the voltage against 1 V, so mV/Pa = 1000 x 10 to the (dBV/20) and the page converts the unit it was given before doing anything else. Levels in dBu are referenced to 0.775 V, so a microphone whose sensitivity is S volts per pascal puts out 20 log10(S / 0.775) + (SPL - 94) dBu at a source level of SPL decibels. The preamp adds its gain in decibels, and the interface reaches full scale at the level it quotes as its maximum input, so the converter level in dBFS is the level after the preamp minus that figure and the headroom is the distance back to zero. The gain that puts a peak on the target is target + maximum input - microphone output, and the source level that reaches the target at the gain entered is the same expression rearranged; the clipping ceiling is the loudest source the input still accepts at that gain. Inputs are accepted from 0.05 to 200 mV/Pa or -86.1 to -13.9 dBV/Pa of sensitivity, 20 to 180 dB SPL, 0 to 80 dB of gain, -20 to 30 dBu of maximum input and a target between -40 and 0 dBFS, decimal commas are accepted, and blank fields, text, a zero or negative sensitivity and values outside those bounds are refused rather than clamped. The page models levels only. It does not know the microphone's self-noise or the preamplifier's equivalent input noise, so it cannot predict a signal-to-noise ratio; it treats every level as a peak, so an RMS or averaged reading needs its own crest factor; and it does not model converter alignment tolerance, a pad or EQ placed before the preamp, input-impedance loading, or whether the result sounds good. Nothing is measured, recorded or sent.

sources.title: Analog Devices, Understanding Microphone Sensitivity (Analog Dialogue 46-02) — 94 dB SPL equals 1 Pa, and mV/Pa converts to dBV by 20 log10 against the 1 V/Pa reference
Biamp Cornerstone, Microphone sensitivity — mic output voltage at the 94 dB SPL reference, dBu against 0.775 V and dBu = dBV + 2.21
